lessons.title: TechCorp Employee Badge Printer
lessons.instructions:
## TechCorp Employee Badge Printer

TechCorp Employee Badge Printer

HR needs a badge formatter for the new hire orientation. Given an employee profile,

build the badge text printed on their lanyard.

Format (exactly):

```

[ID-00042] Priya Sharma | Engineering | MANAGER

```

Rules:



- ID is zero-padded to 5 digits (e.g. employeeId 42 → "00042")

- If isManager is true, suffix is "MANAGER"; otherwise "STAFF"

- department is used as-is (already validated)



@param profile the employee profile

@return formatted badge string

lessons.instructions:
## GreenBasket Grocery Listings

GreenBasket Grocery Listings

You're building product cards for an online grocery app. Each card shows the item name,

stock quantity, line total, and whether it's organic.

Format (exactly):

```

Organic Tomatoes x3 = $4.50

Regular Milk x2 = $6.00

```

Rules:



- Line total = quantity × unitPrice, shown with 2 decimal places

- Prefix "Organic " when isOrganic is true; otherwise "Regular "

- Use String.format for the price part: "%.2f"



@param item the product item

@return formatted listing line

lessons.instructions:
## Bistro 42 Bill Calculator

Bistro 42 Bill Calculator

Waitstaff use this to print the final bill. Given the food subtotal, apply tax and tip.

Rules:



- Tax rate is 8% of subtotal

- Tip is 15% of (subtotal + tax)

- Final total = subtotal + tax + tip, rounded to nearest cent using Math.round(total * 100) / 100.0

- If subtotal is negative, return -1.0



@param subtotal food subtotal in dollars

@return final bill total, or -1.0 for invalid input

lessons.title: FlashSale Discount Engine
lessons.instructions:
## FlashSale Discount Engine

FlashSale Discount Engine

An e-commerce site runs flash sales. Given the original price and discount percentage,

return the sale price.

Rules:



- salePrice = originalPrice × (1 - discountPercent / 100.0)

- Round to 2 decimal places: Math.round(price * 100) / 100.0

- If originalPrice is negative or discountPercent is not between 0 and 100 inclusive, return -1.0



@param originalPrice original price in dollars

@param discountPercent discount percentage (0–100)

@return sale price, or -1.0 for invalid input

lessons.title: StreamTime Video Duration Parser
lessons.instructions:
## StreamTime Video Duration Parser

StreamTime Video Duration Parser

A video platform stores clip length in total seconds. Convert to hours, minutes, and seconds

for the UI player.

Rules:



- hours = totalSeconds / 3600

- minutes = (totalSeconds % 3600) / 60

- seconds = totalSeconds % 60

- If totalSeconds is negative, return null



@param totalSeconds total duration in seconds

@return TimeParts record, or null for invalid input

package com.chaicode.conditionals; /** * City Central Parking * *

City Central Parking garage is the busiest in downtown. They need an * automated system to calculate parking fees. Different vehicle types * have different rates, and there's a daily maximum so customers * aren't overcharged. * *

Rates (first hour / each additional hour): *

    *
  • "car": $5 first hour, then $3/hour
    • *
  • "motorcycle": $3 first hour, then $2/hour
    • *
  • "bus": $10 first hour, then $7/hour
    • *
* *

Daily Maximum (fee can never exceed this): *

    *
  • "car": $30
    • *
  • "motorcycle": $18
    • *
  • "bus": $60
    • *
* *

Rules: *

    *
  • Partial hours are rounded UP (e.g., 1.5 hours → 2 hours)
    • *
  • The fee should never exceed the daily maximum
    • *
  • If hours is 0 or negative, return -1
    • *
  • If vehicleType is not "car", "motorcycle", or "bus", return -1
    • *
* *

Examples: *

    *
  • car, 1 hour → $5
    • *
  • car, 3 hours → $5 + $3 + $3 = $11
    • *
  • car, 0.5 hours → rounds up to 1 hour → $5
    • *
  • car, 24 hours → $5 + 23×$3 = $74 → capped at $30
    • *
* * @param hours number of hours parked * @param vehicleType "car", "motorcycle", or "bus" * @return parking fee or -1 for invalid input */ public final class ParkingFee { private ParkingFee() {} public static int calculateParkingFee(double hours, String vehicleType) { // Your code here return 0; } }

package com.chaicode.conditionals; /** * Sam's Tax Calculator * *

Sam is a freelance graphic designer who dreads tax season every year. * Help Sam by building a tax calculator that uses progressive tax brackets. * *

How progressive tax works: * You don't pay the same rate on ALL your income. Each "slice" of income * is taxed at its own rate: * *

    *
  • Bracket 1: $0 – $10,000 → 0% (tax-free!)
    • *
  • Bracket 2: $10,001 – $30,000 → 10% (only on the amount ABOVE $10,000)
    • *
  • Bracket 3: $30,001 – $70,000 → 20% (only on the amount ABOVE $30,000)
    • *
  • Bracket 4: Over $70,000 → 30% (only on the amount ABOVE $70,000)
    • *
* *

Examples: *

    *
  • Income $8,000 → Tax = $0 (all in bracket 1)
    • *
  • Income $20,000 → Tax = 10% of ($20,000 - $10,000) = $1,000
    • *
  • Income $50,000 → Tax = $2,000 + 20% of ($50,000 - $30,000) = $6,000
    • *
  • Income $100,000 → Tax = $2,000 + $8,000 + 30% of ($100,000 - $70,000) = $19,000
    • *
* *

Rules: *

    *
  • If income is 0 or negative, return 0
    • *
* * @param income annual income in dollars * @return total tax amount owed */ public final class TaxCalculator { private TaxCalculator() {} public static double calculateTax(double income) { // Your code here return 0; } }

- tipPercentage: the percentage as a number (e.g., 15)

- tipAmount: the calculated tip rounded to 2 decimal places

- totalAmount: bill + tip rounded to 2 decimal places



Rules:



- If billAmount is 0 or negative, return null

- If serviceRating is not an integer from 1 to 5, return null



Example:

{@code calculateTip(50, 4) → { tipPercentage: 20, tipAmount: 10.00, totalAmount: 60.00 }}

@param billAmount the bill amount in dollars

@param serviceRating service rating from 1 to 5 (must be a whole number)

@return tip breakdown or null for invalid input

## TrailBuddy - The Hiking Weather App

TrailBuddy - The Hiking Weather App

You're building a weather advisory feature for TrailBuddy, a popular

hiking app used by thousands of outdoor enthusiasts. Based on the

temperature (in Celsius) and whether it's raining, the app should

display helpful advice to hikers.

Advisory Rules (check in this exact order):



- temp >= 35              → "Too hot for hiking - stay indoors and hydrate"

- temp >= 25 and no rain  → "Great weather for hiking - don't forget sunscreen"

- temp >= 25 and raining  → "Warm but rainy - consider indoor activities"

- temp >= 15 and no rain  → "Perfect hiking weather - enjoy the trails"

- temp >= 15 and raining  → "Cool and rainy - bring waterproof gear if hiking"

- temp >= 5 and no rain   → "Chilly - wear layers for your hike"

- temp >= 5 and raining   → "Cold and wet - best to stay indoors"

- temp < 5                → "Too cold - stay warm indoors"



@param temperature temperature in Celsius

@param isRaining whether it's currently raining

@return the weather advisory message
